Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier — attaching the vendor tax packet so we can get a PO in place. Novum is a US-registered operating subsidiary of Novum Global Holdings (foreign parent). For the PO, our operating entity is Novum, Inc. (EIN: 82-XXXXXXX) — we attached the completed W-9 for that entity.

We also attached a W-8BEN-E for the parent entity (Novum Global Holdings) because some invoices will be billed from the parent for international services; I want to be transparent about lineage in case that affects how you set up the supplier profile.

Attachments: Novum_Inc_W9_filled.pdf (W-9), Novum_Global_W8BEN-E.pdf (parent W-8BEN-E), Novum_bank_letter_dated_20261110.pdf (bank letter showing EIN).

Questions:
- Do you need an unredacted EIN on the W-9 or is the redacted SSN block acceptable?
- Will Redwood accept the bank letter as secondary EIN verification, or do you require an IRS CP575/letter?

Happy to provide whatever you need — if helpful I can loop our procurement contact Marco (copied).

Best,
Sana Patel
Vendor Operations Lead
Novum Health

Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: Novum tax forms and PO kickoff

Sana — thanks, got the packet. Two quick clarifications from procurement/accounting before we can move the vendor into our PO queue: 

1) Please confirm the legal entity you want the PO issued to (Novum, Inc. or Novum Global Holdings). If invoices will come from both, we need separate supplier records and a clear mapping in the notes.

2) Regarding the W-9: we need the EIN displayed in full on the W-9 form itself. Redacted SSNs (for sole proprietor SSNs) are fine to hide, but the employer EIN must be present.

3) For EIN verification, we prefer an IRS CP575 or a bank letter showing the EIN. The bank letter you attached is acceptable as provisional evidence; accounting may still request an IRS letter for final verification.

Next steps: Laura (procurement) will confirm whether we create a single supplier profile with multiple billing locations or two distinct vendors. David (accounting) — can you confirm whether the bank letter suffices for a provisional PO? If yes, Vivek can approve a provisional PO that gets finalized after an IRS document is provided.

I attached our vendor onboarding checklist to speed this up.

Thanks,
Vivek
Sr. Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
attachments: [redwood_vendor_onboarding_checklist.pdf]

Sana — appreciate the fast turnaround and the updated W-9. A couple of accounting requirements to finalize supplier setup: 

• For the PO to be approved for payment we need either an IRS CP575 (preferred) OR a notarized bank letter that explicitly lists the EIN and the legal name. The bank letter you provided looks good, but can you confirm whether it was notarized? If not notarized we can accept it temporarily for a provisional PO but final payment will require IRS evidence.

• Please complete the vendor tax attestations in our vendor portal (link below) so we can mark tax classification and withholding rules. If the parent invoices are routed under a different tax classification, we need a separate supplier profile and to set the correct withholding flags.

Portal link: https://procurement.redwood.internal/tickets/PR-7241 — use the "Vendor Evidence" tab and upload the bank letter + W-9.

If provisional PO works for you, we will issue PO-98123 with a "provisional" tag; the PO will move to final status upon receipt of the CP575 or a notarized bank letter. Expected timeline: provisional PO within 24 business hours after portal upload; finalization within 7–10 business days after IRS verification.

Thanks,
David Kim
Manager, Accounting — Redwood Inference
